outcome: INTERRUPTED — Colab runtime disconnected, ephemeral /content lost
note: This is NOT a completed 2000-step experiment and must not be reported as one. It establishes T4 feasibility to ~step 500 and an early learning trend. It says nothing about final model quality.

memory.note: The corrected estimator predicted 3.57 GiB for this configuration and the run fit comfortably. Peak VRAM was not captured before the disconnect, so the estimate remains unvalidated against a measured peak.

throughput.note: approximate, as reported in the session

termination.consequence: the ephemeral /content filesystem was reclaimed, taking every checkpoint and the metrics log with it. Nothing was recoverable.

what_this_proves: the revised 94.48M configuration trains on a Tesla T4 without OOM
throughput is ~2100 tokens/s with gradient checkpointing on
the model is learning: validation BPB fell from 1.317 to 1.279 between steps 200 and 400
1.279 BPB at step 400 is already far below the 8.0 uniform-byte baseline
what_this_does_not_prove: final model quality — the run covered ~25% of the configured 2000 steps
that the loss curve continues to fall
measured peak VRAM against the 3.57 GiB estimate
anything about distillation or teacher capability retention
why_it_could_not_be_resumed: checkpoints were written non-atomically, so any in-flight write was corrupt
checkpoints held weights and a step counter but no scheduler, GradScaler, RNG or data position, so a resume would have restarted the one-cycle schedule and rewound the data to epoch 0
nothing was copied off the ephemeral filesystem
there was no pointer identifying the newest valid checkpoint
resolution: Phase 2B: atomic checkpoints with a COMPLETE marker and a verified latest.json pointer, full state capture (scheduler, scaler, RNG, data position, tokens seen), lightweight progress records independent of checkpoints, `--resume latest`, and Drive persistence that refuses to copy an incomplete checkpoint.
